correctness.rationale: Using the even-weight 5-bit model fixes the degree-five Clebsch graph: 16 vertices, 40 edges, SRG(16,5,0,2). Rebuilt ordinary independence faces by forbidden distance-4 pairs and checked all 393 including empty, face vector (16,80,160,120,16). A sequential vertex-toggle Hasse matching on all nonempty faces leaves 191 pairs, one critical 0-cell, nine critical 3-cells, and global acyclicity of all 1200 oriented incidences (392 visited vertices); hence Forman implies integral wedge of nine S3, not only field Betti ranks. Verified all 16×120=1920 affine maps are graph symmetries and independently recomputed the reduced signed Lefschetz trace of every map. It equals sgn(pi)(fixed(pi)-1+sum_{fixed i}(-1)^{a_i}), and the source verifier additionally checks orbit-based traces, E_even Fourier multiplicities 4 and five ones, and the averaged S5 standard 4-d module. Thus the degree-3 rational module is the asserted signed 4⊕5; no equivariant wedge or integral module lattice is claimed.
residual_risks: Acyclic discrete-Morse matching proves nonequivariant homotopy; the equivariant calculation is at rational homology level only.
The 16 even-bit coordinate presentation must not be confused with the 10-regular complementary Clebsch graph.
